ORIGINAL FULL BRIEF:
# W008 — implicit four-list additive collision detection

2026-10-08. Parent proposal, PROVISIONAL pending independent audit. No
candidate execution, code or Lean change, or new factoring bound.

This branch replaces repeated concentration-map training with four directly
sampled uniform lists. Useful supply is elementary; the selected question is
the actual computation that detects it without expanding both pair lists.

## Paid generator and an exact candidate success calculation

Promise initially N=pq, distinct odd primes p<q. Generate four independent
lists A,B,C,D, each containing K independent uniform residues modulo N.
Sampling costs O(K) residues, no factors or local group orders.

For each tuple t=(i,j,k,l), define
L_t=a_i+b_j-c_k-d_l modulo N. Let I_t indicate p divides L_t but q does not.
Its mean is a=(1/p)(1-1/q). Any two distinct tuples give linearly independent
linear forms in the 4K input coordinates over each prime field: their supports
differ and every coefficient is nonzero. Their two values are therefore
independent uniform residues over each field. CRT then makes I_t,I_u pairwise
independent, despite shared list entries. Thus, with Z=sum_t I_t,

    lambda=E Z=K^4*a,
    E Z^2=lambda^2+lambda*(1-a),
    Pr[Z>0] >= lambda/(lambda+1-a).

This is a proposed exact second-moment argument, not an iid model for all
K^4 tuples. At K about p^(1/4), it gives constant useful-collision mass.
A tuple that vanishes modulo N is a global duplicate and is not useful.
Its total occurrence probability is at most K^4/N by a union bound.

## Actual scalar object and a full-gcd localization procedure

For monic input polynomials F_A(T)=product_i(T-a_i), etc., define

    S_AB(T)=Res_X(F_A(X),F_B(T-X))
           =product_(i,j)(T-a_i-b_j),
    S_CD(T)=product_(k,l)(T-c_k-d_l),
    R(A,B,C,D)=Res_T(S_AB(T),S_CD(T)).

Up to an irrelevant sign, R is product_t L_t. The target is its residue
modulo N, not an exponentially large exact integer.

If gcd(R,N) is proper, return it. If it is 1, this trial fails. If it is N,
partition one non-singleton original list into two parts. The two child
products multiply to the parent. Evaluate the first child:
proper gcd returns; gcd N descends there; gcd 1 descends into the other
child whose gcd is then N. Repeat, splitting original lists, down to a
single tuple. Reaching a tuple with gcd N is declared a failed trial, not
a factor. There is no restart into every sibling.

On the event that no tuple is globally zero, such a full-gcd descent cannot
reach a full-gcd leaf. If some useful tuple exists, the root has gcd p or N
and the procedure must recover a proper factor. This probabilistic extractor
therefore avoids globally deduplicating K^2 pair sums: it may fail on a
global duplicate, whose total probability was bounded above. This is a
different recovery rule from claiming arbitrary deterministic full-gcd
backtracking succeeds.

With p,q>=131, the first power-of-two K with K^4>=p has K^4<16p.
The useful-event lower bound exceeds 0.49, while the global-duplicate bound
is at most 16/q<1/8. Hence success exceeds 1/3 at that stage.
An N-only schedule doubles K up to the first K with K^4>=ceil(sqrt(N)),
then repeats that capped stage. For all stages from the useful threshold
to this cap, lambda is at least the threshold value and
K^4/N<16/sqrt(N)<=16/p; the same lower bound works.
A fixed number of independent trials per stage makes the geometric
expected-cost tail summable for a detector with any fixed power exponent.
Small primes up to 127 can be removed at constant setup cost.
This is still only the stated squarefree semiprime scope.

## What the supplied algorithms actually cost

1. Explicit pair-list control: form K^2 sums per side, then apply a paid
   scalar version of the W006 batch detector or ordinary product trees.
   Cost K^2*poly(log N+log K), not K. At the threshold this is
   sqrt(p)*poly(log N), a known scale.

2. Newton/composed-sum construction: for degree d=K^2, compute power sums
   of the K roots up to order d from the reciprocal input polynomials'
   logarithmic derivatives. The exponential-generating-series identity is

       s_m(AB)=sum_(r=0)^m binom(m,r) s_r(A)s_(m-r)(B).

   Form S_AB and S_CD through Newton/exponential series, then their scalar
   resultant. This actually shares the K^4 term product; it still writes
   Theta(K^2) coefficients and does not save the critical quadratic cost.
   The exact quasi-linear-in-d algorithm and ring conditions require audit.

   Integer divisions 1,...,d in these formulas must be charged: test
   gcd(d!,N). A proper gcd is an early factor; gcd N triggers bounded
   product-tree localization among the explicit integers 1,...,d or a
   declared failed chart. If the gcd is 1 these integers are units and all
   indicated divisions are legal. Computing this product in O(d) work
   does not spoil the d-scale bound. Nonunit polynomial pivots in a fast
   resultant must similarly produce factors or be handled correctly.
   Do not import a field algorithm without these conditions.

Primary source to inspect: Bostan, Flajolet, Salvy, Schost,
Fast Computation of Special Resultants (2006), author copy
https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/~eschost/publications/BoFlSaSc05.pdf .
Parent opened the paper and read search/intro material; the full theorem
scope is NOT yet accepted. The explicit power-sum identity above is derived
algebraically. No source claim of a subquadratic-in-K scalar detector.

## A materially different attempted saving: visible modular filtering

Use auxiliary M coprime to N (gcd-tested) and draw each input uniformly
modulo MN. Then the auxiliary labels modulo M are independent of ALL CRT
data modulo N. Reduce only the residue payload modulo N.

Keep A+B pairs with auxiliary sum 0 and independently keep C+D pairs
with auxiliary sum 0. Each retained list has expected size L=K^2/M.
Conditional on labels the hidden-p tests still have their original
probabilities. The expected useful-tuple count is

    K^4/M^2 * (1/p)(1-1/q).

To retain constant success via this count one still needs K^2/M of
order sqrt(p), and explicit surviving-pair traffic already costs that
much. A matched-bucket variant retaining all pair sums has K^2 traffic
and loses a factor M in the number of tested quadruples, so it does not
improve the exponent either. This closes these INDEPENDENT-label filters,
not all filters correlated with arithmetic structure. Ordinary low bits
of residues sampled only modulo N need a separate dependence argument;
they are not silently identified with this exact CRT experiment.

## Conditional consequence and limited hardness connection

An actual uniform evaluator for R on arbitrary sublists of size at most K
in K^alpha*poly(log N+log K) bit work, with alpha<2, plus the displayed
O(log K) localization and paid sampling, would give expected
p^(alpha/4)*poly(log N) splitting on distinct odd semiprimes. This would
improve the p^1/2 collision control. It is NOT a supplied algorithm and
does not by itself improve heuristic NFS or rigorous subexponential
general factoring. No degree/output-size lower bound is claimed for a
scalar-only computation.

An exact scalar-R algorithm on arbitrary lists and prime moduli also
decides ordinary four-list integer sum equality: for inputs of magnitude
at most B choose a prime ell>4B. A term is 0 mod ell exactly when it is the
integer zero; the full product vanishes iff such a tuple exists.
This is only a reduction, not an imported 4SUM conjecture/lower bound.
It does NOT apply unchanged to a detector returning only proper factors,
or to a method proved solely for random lists.

Next constructive question: can the scalar-only computation exploit the
random-list promise, or actual shared algebraic structure, to go below
K^2 without the explicitly expanded degree-K^2 intermediate? The standard
Newton computation and independent visible filtering do not do so.
Merely naming a resultant evaluator is not progress; require an explicit
algorithm, with full-gcd recovery and the paid generator intact.


Audit priorities:
1. Verify pairwise independence for all different index tuples (shared coordinates, small fields, cross-prime CRT), success lower bound, global duplicate loss, one-path localization and N-only doubling/cap/repeat schedule. Give rigorous bound with safe constants; flag every promise limitation. Do not assume K^4 independent events.
2. Work out an ACTUAL ordinary-ring K^2*poly(logN+logK) control from the power-series identity and fast composed sums. Read exact relevant theorem assumptions from the primary author paper; track denominators and fast-resultant nonunits/full gcds. If it needs a repair, supply it. Do not turn materialization size into a scalar-computation lower bound.
3. Verify independent auxiliary-label filtering count/traffic and its precise scope. Do not extend it to arbitrary nonindependent filters.
4. Audit the conditional subquadratic consequence and the limited exact-scalar-to-integer-4SUM reduction. No novelty claims or conjectural lower bounds imported from search snippets. Distinguish worst-case exact scalar routines from randomized useful-factor-only routines.
5. Constructive challenge: if you find a real algebraic replacement for the K^2 intermediate on this random-input promise, spell it out and charge it. Otherwise identify exactly which existing computation fails to save work; no renamed oracle.

Save source read scope and verified hashes. No experiment is requested because the decisive gates are symbolic. Report exact dispositions, corrections and the next concrete computation worth trying.

NEW EXCLUSIVE AFFINE GRID NOTE:
# W008 — affine random grids with a paid block evaluator

2026-10-08. Parent constructive alternative, PROVISIONAL. No experiment,
new solver/Lean code or established factoring improvement. W008 A continues
on arbitrary random lists; this note changes the generator to five random
residues and adds structure to the scalar product.

## Five random parameters, K^4 local tests

Choose b,a_1,a_2,a_3,a_4 independently uniformly modulo N=pq, p<q odd
distinct primes. For v in {0,...,K-1}^4 let

    L_v=b+sum_i a_i*v_i  mod N.

The array is described by five residues and K; no K-list expansion is
needed merely to specify it. For K<=p, different v,w are distinct modulo
both p and q. The linear forms in the five random parameters have
coefficient vectors (1,v) and (1,w), which cannot be scalar multiples
over either prime field. Thus the candidate pairwise-independent useful
indicator law of W008 holds verbatim:

    a=(1/p)(1-1/q),
    lambda=K^4*a,
    Pr[some p-only zero] >= lambda/(lambda+1-a).

Global-zero probability is at most K^4/N. The shared random offset is
essential to this simple proof. Without it, scalar-proportional index
vectors give dependent events and v=0 is always a global zero. No
primitive-vector enumeration is needed with b present.

At the first power-of-two K with K^4>=p, K<=p for p>=2, and K^4<16p.
For p,q>=131 the same provisional constant success (>1/3) after the
one-path full-gcd descent follows. Descents restrict coordinate intervals
and translate b; the compact representation is preserved.

The pairwise-independence assertion is NOT silently extended to K>p.
A schedule may be proved separately or use a paid dovetail across scales;
the old arbitrary-list monotonic probability argument needs rechecking.
There is no hidden factor input to this generator.

## Exact block product over the composite ring

Write R_K(b,a)=product_v L_v modulo N. First suppose K=m*h exactly.
Write every coordinate v_i=r_i+m*q_i, with 0<=r_i<m, 0<=q_i<h.
Build the single-variable monic polynomial

    F(T)=product_(r in [0,m)^4) (T+sum_i a_i*r_i).

Evaluate it at all h^4 points

    x_q=b+m*sum_i a_i*q_i.

Then R_K is exactly product_q F(x_q). This is a real algorithm: enumerate
m^4 inner shifts, build their monic product tree, enumerate h^4 outer
points, perform monic remainder-tree evaluation, and multiply the results.
No field interpolation or inverses of differences are required. Using
fast modular polynomial arithmetic its work is

    (m^4+h^4)*poly(log N+log K),

with the coefficient, point and output records counted. With m,h near
sqrt(K), it costs K^2*poly(log N+log K). For powers of two, choose m as
2^floor(log2(K)/2), leaving h/m at most 2.

Arbitrary rectangular subboxes used in recovery are handled by splitting
individual coordinate lengths into blocks plus remainders, at most 2^4
types per chosen split. Alternatively pad a requested interval by a
dyadic decomposition and multiply the O(log(K)^4) subbox products. The
subbox construction and all factors are charged; no extra leaves may be
silently included.

This supplies a composite-ring control without constructing the two
degree-K^2 composed-sum polynomials or using factorial denominators.
It does NOT reduce the critical exponent. Within this materialized
single-block scheme, m^4+h^4>=2K^2, so changing the split cannot help.
This is a restriction on these actual records, not on every algorithm.

## Why an obvious small-order shift recurrence fails generically

Let G_K(X)=product_(v in [0,K)^4)(X+sum_i a_i*v_i) over Q(a_1,...,a_4).
All K^4 roots are distinct. For a nonzero integer vector h, put gamma=a·h.
The number of common roots of G_K(X+gamma) and G_K(X) is

    I(h)=product_i max(0,K-|h_i|).

After cancelling their gcd, both numerator and denominator of
G_K(X+gamma)/G_K(X) have degree K^4-I(h). For a nonzero shift this is
at least K^3: a unit coordinate shift attains equality. A shift not
equal to a difference of grid roots has no cancellation at all.

Hence this family does not supply a scalar FIRST-ORDER shift equation
with bounded-degree polynomial numerator and denominator through
ordinary cancellation. The surviving face is large. Treating that
degree as a constant inside a matrix-factorial/holonomic algorithm is
invalid. This does not exclude higher-order recurrences, a compact
face evaluator, specialization-specific identities, nonlinear changes,
or calculations existing only modulo N.

The proof over independent symbolic slopes is not a statement that four
rational numbers are Q-linearly independent. For an integer specialization
it applies only when distinct relevant bounded coefficient vectors have
distinct dot products. Small-base or aligned slopes may fail that condition.
In particular a_i=a*K^(i-1) makes the full box an ordinary length-K^4
arithmetic progression: it has a different shift overlap, but its standard
factorial evaluator again has square-root-of-length K^2 cost.

## Complete costs and a different next computation

Source input traffic is now O(log N+log K) for fixed dimension, so an
arbitrary-list input-size objection or worst-case 4SUM reduction cannot
simply be imposed on this compact promise. The actual product algorithm
still writes K^2 records. To change the conclusion, produce a scalar-only
grid algorithm below K^2 with setup, modular bit widths and the O(log K)
recovery calls included. No such algorithm is supplied here.

Primary leads for the precise recurrence-computation scope:
- Bostan--Yurkevich, Fast Computation of the N-th Term of a q-Holonomic
  Sequence and Applications, https://arxiv.org/abs/2012.08656 .
- The accepted H029/H030 files already distinguish fast monic product
  computation from output-size obstructions. Do not duplicate their
  nonpolynomial Lehman floor-root representation audit; this grid has
  exact affine leaves and a different random generator.

A review should prove/correct the generator and boundary count, give
the paid rectangular product/recovery bound, and check whether an
existing constant-order recurrence theorem actually applies. Do not
call a multiple-gamma symbol or a general norm a fast modular evaluator.


Preserve source read scope and hashes. Return exact corrections, strongest scoped result and the next constructive gate. No experiments authorized.

1. **The N-only schedule had a gap, now repaired.** For unbalanced N (say p ≈ 2²⁰, q ≈ 2¹⁰⁰⁰), the capped stage has K ≈ N^(1/8), far above p. Pairwise independence fails there, so the note's "same lower bound" step doesn't hold. A separate argument covers K ≥ p:
   - If a₁ is a unit mod p (probability ≥ 1−1/p), then as v₁ runs through a full residue range, some point is a p-zero.
   - The global-zero bound K⁴/N needs only uniform marginals, so it holds at every K.
   - Every stage from the threshold up to the cap then succeeds with probability ≥ 0.378.
   - With 4 trials per stage the expected cost converges (4·(2/3)⁴ ≈ 0.79 < 1). With 3 it isn't certified (about 1.0002).
   - Result: expected O(√p · poly(log N)), Las Vegas, without knowing p.
2. **Block-product constant.** The note's single split m = 2^⌊log₂K/2⌋ gives 4.25K² records when log₂K is odd. Splitting each coordinate separately reaches exactly 2K², which is the floor for this scheme. It also needs no padding or extra leaves.
3. **Recovery costs no extra log K.** Each box in the descent is half the previous one and costs O(√|B|), so the whole descent adds at most about 7.3K² records.
4. **The overlap count only bounds specialised slopes.** The symbolic count I(h) = Πᵢ max(0, K−|hᵢ|) is right, but for actual slope values the reduced degree K⁴−I(h) is only an upper bound. I give an exact sufficient condition for equality. More importantly, at the operating scale (K⁴ > p) the grid always has repeated roots mod p. Those coincidences depend on the hidden p, so the symbolic statement only rules out identities that hold for generic slopes.

**What's confirmed:**
- The pairwise-independent law for K ≤ p, which is why the random offset b matters.
- The global-zero union bound.
- Success > 1/3 at the threshold (≥ 0.381).
- The full-gcd descent invariant.
- The ring-generic monic block product over Z/N, with every cost item you listed charged.

**Bostan–Yurkevich (arXiv 2012.08656v1):** it covers sequences with a single index over a field, built from powers of q with q ≠ 1, at cost about √(N·d). The grid's terms are additive, so only the q = 1 analogues (Chudnovsky; Bostan–Gaudry–Schost 2007) apply. Slicing along one coordinate gives an exact recurrence of length K and degree K³, costing √(K⁴) = K². I also proved that for this sequence no higher-order recurrence can have degree below K³, when the recurrence is a symbolic identity. If a recurrence only needs to hold on the finite range, low-degree ones always exist by interpolation, but finding their coefficients is the original problem. So BY doesn't beat K².

**Next constructive gate:** the only route I didn't close is writing R = Πₙ c(n), where c has low degree in n but high degree in b, and each c(n) is a full product over a separate part of the grid that is cheaper to compute than its size. A concrete design must give that family explicitly, prove the identity symbolically, pay for finding the coefficients below K², and keep the success law and descent. It can be falsified by a symbolic check at K = 2 or 4. Lipton (ANTS 1994) connects this to short straight-line programs for polynomials with many rational roots; I read only that paper's abstract.

Files are in `research/findings`:
- W008-affine-grid-review.md
- W008-affine-grid-review-delivery.sha256
- W008-affine-grid-review-sources/ (BY PDF, text extract and abstract page, all hashed)

The only computation was exact arithmetic checking the threshold constants. There were no candidate runs, and no shared-state, solver, Lean or commit changes.

Sources:
- [Bostan–Yurkevich, arXiv 2012.08656](https://arxiv.org/abs/2012.08656)
- [Lipton 1994, LNCS 877](https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/3-540-58691-1_45)

Read section 9 of W008-fourlist-review.md as original motivation; do not redo its probability/bit-cost review. # W008 — two compact factors can destroy the Hankel displacement state

2026-10-08. Parent derivation, PROVISIONAL pending independent audit.
This develops the actual multiplication gate selected in section 9 of
[the four-list review](W008-fourlist-review.md). No candidate run, solver or
Lean change, and no factoring bound.

## Proposed saving and the operation tested

In Q=R[X,Y]/(F_C(X),F_D(Y)), one input factor is
H_b=F_A(X+Y-b). For degree-K monic F_A, its coefficient array C becomes
Hankel after scaling Ctilde_rs=r!s! C_rs, apart from the pure-variable
boundary changes caused by reduction. Consequently
Delta(Ctilde)=J Ctilde-Ctilde J^T, with J the downward shift, has bounded
rank for a single factor. A rank-r generator stored as U V^T uses O(Kr)
entries. The hoped-for computation was to update short generators under
quotient multiplication, then obtain the determinant norm without writing
K^2 coefficients.

Here is an explicit two-factor obstruction to maintaining this same
low-displacement-rank representation. This is not a lower bound for an
implicit formula, a different displacement operator, or the scalar norm.

## Exact family, no search

Take K>=2 over Q and specialize

    F_A(T)=T^K,  b_1=b_2=0,
    F_C(X)=X^K-1,  F_D(Y)=Y^K.

Each factor H=(X+Y)^K mod (X^K-1,Y^K) has the single-factor structure
above. Their product is the residue of (X+Y)^(2K). Its only nonzero
coefficients are

    C_00=1,
    C_(r,K-r)=binom(2K,K+r),  1<=r<=K-1.

Indeed powers of Y at least K vanish. Terms with X exponent K+r,
1<=r<=K-1, reduce to X^r Y^(K-r), while X^(2K) reduces to 1.
The term with X exponent K has Y exponent K and vanishes.

After factorial scaling put

    w_r=(2K)! r!/(K+r)!,  1<=r<=K-1.

Thus Ctilde_00=1 and Ctilde_(r,K-r)=w_r. Its displacement has the
top-left block [[0,-1],[1,0]]. On rows and columns 2,...,K-1 its only
nonzero entries lie on r+s=K+1 and are

    Delta_(r,K+1-r)=w_(r-1)-w_r
                         =K (2K)! (r-1)!/(K+r)! > 0.

The two blocks do not interact. Therefore

    det Delta = (-1)^((K-2)(K-3)/2)
                product_(r=2)^(K-1) [K (2K)! (r-1)!/(K+r)!] != 0.

For K=2 the product is empty and det Delta=1. Hence this displacement
has rank exactly K after only two multiplicative updates. An explicit
rank-factor generator U,V consequently needs quadratic-size arrays.

The specialization F_C=X^K-1 need not split over Q. It is a valid
symbolic quotient-algebra certificate: its nonzero determinant proves
that the determinant polynomial in monic F_A,F_C,F_D and shifts is not
identically zero. Substitution of elementary symmetric polynomials in
formal list roots is injective, so generic split-list inputs also have
full displacement rank. This does not assert a useful probability over
the finite fields at the factoring scale, nor a bound on modular
exceptional characteristics. Repeated A entries and equal shifts in the
certificate are permitted by the original arbitrary-list contract.

## What has and has not been removed

The failed assumption is closure of a single Hankel displacement
description under multiplication after the two quotient reductions.
The input factors individually remain compact. A scheme that explicitly
stores arbitrary K-by-r generator arrays loses the desired saving as
soon as it encounters this family. The special full-rank displacement
above itself has a short anti-diagonal formula, so full rank is emphatically
not a lower bound for every representation or every input-specific program.

Two changed computations are outside the calculation:

1. Keep the product as a list/tree of its original compact factors and
   update the scalar determinant norm without forming their product's
   generator. Norm multiplicativity is an identity, not such an update:
   the cost of computing each factor's norm and sharing those computations
   across all shifts still has to be supplied.
2. Choose a displacement operator adapted to both quotient polynomials
   and retain its generators under multiplication. The usual fact that
   all multiplication matrices commute is insufficient: zero commutator
   does not provide a cheap determinant. Give an explicit norm algorithm
   as well as a closed representation.

Neither change currently has a sub-K^2 algorithm. The next cheap test is
independent symbolic verification of this determinant and its precise
scope. Do not run a factoring screen to test a characteristic-zero identity.


Return a precise acceptance/correction and, if the claimed obstruction is valid, inspect ONE concrete escape computation: an operator adapted to the two quotient reductions, or scalar norm updates on a factor tree. Derive an actual update identity and charge required state, all K factors, dimension of multiplication matrices, and norm extraction; do not just name a structured-matrix determinant algorithm. Prefer symbolic falsification if the proposed escape immediately recreates K^2 data. Any prior-art claims require primary-source inspection with read scope and hashes. No full-rank claim may be promoted to a generic arithmetic-circuit, random-input, or factoring lower bound. Keep the report focused; no additional candidate runs.
